query: What does Claudette's behavior suggest about her stance on development and change on Maple Street?
gold: Claudette consistently opposes any planning application that would alter the street's residential character. In Session 1, her immediate response to the no. 22 loft conversion notice was 'This street does not need any more bulk added to it. I shall be objecting.' She frames this in terms of visual impact and preserving the street's character — not noise, not traffic. In Session 3, she linked the traffic danger Marcus experienced to development ('All this traffic is exactly what happens when you allow more development'). Her thirty-year tenure gives her a before-and-after frame that shapes all of her planning opinions.
context:
[1] (about=Claudette, episodic, t0 @2025-05-05T11:17:00) I saw it this morning. I remember when no. 22 was a single-storey cottage. This street does not need any more bulk added to it. I shall be objecting.
[2] (about=Claudette, episodic, t4 @2025-05-19T09:02:00) How frightening. I remember when this was a quiet road. All this traffic is exactly what happens when you allow more development, more occupants, more cars, more danger for our children.
[3] (about=Claudette, episodic, t2 @2025-05-12T18:21:00) a trial period I could live with. Permanence is what irritates me

But £80 a year is an additional burden on residents who have always parked freely here. I remember when you could park outside your own home without paying for the privilege. I am not convinced.

agent_answer: Claudette's behavior suggests she is opposed to and nostalgic about development and change on Maple Street, favoring preservation of the street's quieter, more neighborly character over new building, traffic, and permanent schemes.
